```python
# Pseudo latency-budgeted inference
import time

def classify(tweet, model, classifier):

    emb = model.encode(tweet.text)
    pred = classifier.predict(emb)
    latency = time.time() - t0
    return pred, latency
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes end-to-end design for live, multilingual misinformation detection with tight latency constraints, retrieval-based evidence, and comprehensive auditability.

## Key Concepts
- Streaming NLP and ASR
- Language detection and on-the-fly translation
- Retrieval-Augmented Detection (RAG) and evidence provenance
- Privacy, auditing, drift monitoring, explainability

## Code Example
```python
# Pseudo-structure of streaming pipeline
def process_utterance(utterance):
    text = asr(utterance.audio)
    lang = detect_language(text)
    translated = translate(text, target_lang='en')
    claims = extract_claims(translated)
    evidence = retrieve_evidence(claims)
    scores = compute_confidence(claims, evidence)
    log_interaction(utterance, claims, evidence, scores)
    return claims, evidence, scores
```

## Design Considerations
- **Latency**: Parallel processing, optimized embeddings, and efficient retrieval ensure sub-200ms response
- **Accuracy**: Multilingual ASR quality impacts downstream performance; use ensemble models for language detection
- **Scalability**: Microservices architecture with horizontal scaling for high-throughput scenarios
- **Privacy**: Optional content redaction, user consent mechanisms, and GDPR-compliant data handling
- **Monitoring**: Real-time drift detection on model performance and automated model retraining triggers

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical NLP extraction skills under real-world constraints typical of job platforms.

## Key Concepts
- Multilingual information extraction from user-generated content
- Tiny on-device models, inference optimization, and quantization techniques
- Code-switching handling, data labeling workflows, and privacy-by-design architecture

## Code Example
```javascript
function extractJob(posting) {
  const title = (posting.split('title:')[1] || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
  const location = (posting.split('location:')[1] || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
  const skills = (posting.split('skills:')[1] || '').split('\n')[0].trim();
  const remote = /remote|home.?office|telecommut/i.test(posting);
  const seniority = /senior|junior|lead|manager|intern/i.test(posting) ? 
    posting.match(/senior|junior|lead|manager|intern/i)[0] : 'mid';
  
  return { title, location, skills, remote, seniority };
}
```

## Labeling Plan
- Use heuristic-labeled data from structured job feeds as initial training data
- Apply human-in-the-loop validation for ambiguous cases
- Implement confidence thresholds to route low-confidence extractions to rules or human review

## Latency & Privacy
- On-device inference ensures <100 ms latency with quantized TinyBERT
- No data leaves the device, satisfying privacy requirements

## Offline Evaluation
- Test on held-out multilingual dataset covering all three languages and code-switching scenarios
- Measure precision/recall per field and overall schema completeness

## Staged Rollout
- Phase 1: Rule-based extraction only (baseline)
- Phase 2: Hybrid model + rules on 5% of traffic
- Phase 3: Full rollout with A/B testing and monitoring
